en.title: SEC Reviews ETF Filing Rules as Old Bitcoin Awakens and Bitwise Boosts XRP Holdings
en.body:
The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is re-examining its automated filing pathways for exchange-traded funds after asset managers flooded regulators with proposals for exotic crypto products and event-linked contracts. Wall Street firms have sought approval for funds tied to leveraged returns, election outcomes, and economic indicators, pushing the boundaries of what qualifies as an investable product. The SEC must now determine whether existing processes can handle this surge in creative structuring while maintaining investor protections.

The filing surge coincides with notable whale activity across multiple blockchains. Galaxy Research reported that Bitcoin coins dormant for more than a decade moved at an unusually high pace in 2026, with six ancient wallets shifting approximately $40 million in a single 10-day stretch this month. While such movements often attract speculation about potential selling pressure, the volumes remain a fraction of daily Bitcoin trading volume, which typically exceeds $30 billion across major exchanges.

In the altcoin space, Bitwise continues to demonstrate conviction in XRP despite a pullback from recent highs. The asset manager moved $15.4 million worth of XRP off exchange supply, a maneuver interpreted by analysts as accumulation. The token trades near the $0.55 support level after failing to sustain momentum above $0.65 earlier this month, with the Relative Strength Index hovering around 48, suggesting neither overbought nor oversold conditions.

Separately, crypto executives are grappling with a novel question: what currency will power transactions between AI agents? Industry leaders interviewed by CoinDesk acknowledged widespread agreement that autonomous AI systems will require native payment rails, but consensus on implementation remains elusive. Some argue existing stablecoins could scale to meet demand, while others contend that entirely new protocols better suited for machine-to-machine settlements have not yet been developed.

The convergence of regulatory scrutiny, evolving on-chain behavior, and emerging use cases underscores a market in transition. Institutional players are hedging their positions while regulators attempt to establish guardrails for increasingly complex financial instruments.

Sources: CryptoSlate, Decrypt, U.Today, CoinDesk
